name: Primary Avascular Necrosis

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of osteonecrosis on X-ray or MRI
Presence of joint pain localized to affected site, typically the hip
Exclusion of secondary causes such as trauma, corticosteroid use, or alcohol abuse
Bone scintigraphy showing decreased uptake in affected area

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical symptoms plus radiographic evidence of osteonecrosis with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MRI is the most sensitive imaging modality for early diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized deep groin pain exacerbated by weight-bearing
searchTerms: deep groin pain worsened by walking
localized hip area pain with weight bearing
pain in groin when standing or walking

pathognomonic.symptomName: Limited range of motion of the affected joint

searchTerms: joint stiffness that comes and goes

common.symptomName: Limping gait due to hip involvement

searchTerms: knee pain caused by problems elsewhere
pain felt in knee from another joint
loss of muscle bulk by joint
grating or crackling sound in joints
symptoms of secondary joint wear and tear

rare.symptomName: Systemic constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: general symptoms like low fever and fatigue

laboratory: Exclusion of secondary causes via blood tests (e.g., corticosteroid levels, lipid profile)
imaging: MRI showing subchondral bone marrow edema and necrosis
X-ray showing sclerosis, cystic changes, and eventual femoral head collapse
Bone scintigraphy with decreased uptake in necrotic areas
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified for primary form
other: Histopathology showing dead bone with empty lacunae and surrounding reactive bone

distinguishingFeatures: History of corticosteroid use or alcohol abuse
Diffuse bone marrow edema without necrosis on MRI

redFlags: Sudden worsening of joint pain with inability to bear weight
Rapid progression to femoral head collapse
Signs of joint infection or systemic illness
references: Mankin HJ. Nontraumatic necrosis of bone (osteonecrosis). N Engl J Med. 1992;326(22):1473-1479.
Ficat RP. Idiopathic bone necrosis of the femoral head. Early diagnosis and treatment. J Bone Joint Surg Br. 1985;67(1):3-9.
Mont MA, Hungerford DS. Nontraumatic avascular necrosis of the femoral head. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1995;77(3):459-474.
